title: Eagle view: a new terminal takes the whole empty space it lands in, not half the height
story: In eagle view, a new terminal used to arrive at the size of a tile from the automatic grid, so after Tidy up and closing one terminal, the new one filled only half of the free column. Now a new terminal, or its not-launched card, fills the whole empty space it lands in. Only the eagle view grid changed; Tidy up, resizing, moving and the per-project view work as before.

checks.criterion: In eagle view, after Tidy up, a new card and the terminal it launches take the whole free full-height column.
checks.steps: Start the desktop app and open a made-up project such as demo-alpha. Launch three terminals and switch to eagle view. Press Alt+T. Close the leftmost terminal. Add a new terminal to demo-alpha with the top bar's + button. Launch the new card.
checks.expected: The card and then the launched terminal fill the whole left column, top to bottom (before this change they filled only the top half).

checks.criterion: When no empty space is big enough, the biggest tile still gives up half its room.
checks.steps: In eagle view, arrange two terminals so they cover the whole grid, for example by dragging one onto a screen edge. Add a new terminal.
checks.expected: The biggest terminal splits in half, and the new one takes the freed half.
